title: 1:1 sync notebook — Maya & Diego (API/Console/Dedicated/Private)
content:
Purpose: quick, messy prep for my 1:1 with Diego. Focus areas: API performance anomaly, console rollout checklist, Dedicated capacity contract ask, Private deployment onboarding gaps. Keep this loose — will bring key bullets and action items.

Top priorities to surface (short):
- API latency gap: 95th p50 diverging on long-context agents (large seq > 4k). Confirm hotspots and mitigation (short-term fallback model vs kernel tuning).
- Console: rollout of trace-level UI for per-route latency — must decide MVP telemetry fields and retention.
- Dedicated: approaching Q2 contract renewal window for Acme Corp pilot — need go/no-go on proposed burst autoscaling.
- Private: onboarding checklist missing KMS integration runbook and audit log examples — blocking initial pilot.

Quick numbers to mention (pull from memory + recent dashboards):
- API 95th latency (avg recent week): 420 ms for 1–2048 tokens, but spikes up to 1.2s for >4096 token jobs.
- Error budget burn rate: ~2.4% monthly (threshold 3%).
- Dedicated pool utilization (staging): 68% baseline, 92% peak during internal load test.
- Private pilot candidate count: 3 orgs signed NDAs, 1 completed infra scoping.

Open questions I want Diego to weigh in on:
1) Short-term mitigation for long-context latency spikes: (A) route long-context requests to quantized model variant with >10% CPU savings but slightly lower quality, (B) enable priority prefetching of KV cache + temporary larger batch windows, (C) throttle + client-side guidance. Which would SRE prefer as least risky for production?
2) Console tracing: retention tradeoffs. Default retention 7d vs 30d — cost delta is non-linear. Do we gate 30d behind premium plan or expose sampling?
3) Dedicated autoscale burst: Sales wants burst to 2x baseline for onboarding demos. Risk: cost overruns if misused. Can we implement burst budget with automatic alerts and hard caps? How much engineering effort?
4) Private onboarding friction: KMS patterns vary by customer. Do we publish a generic KMS integration template + one HSM example, or do we ship a small plugin SDK (3–4 days) for common KMS vendors?

Notes to self / what I learned since last 1:1:
- Diego: kernel selection work paid off on small seq perf; bigger seq still losing due to attention implementation and memory paging.
- Diego expressed preference last week for operational knobs rather than product changes for perf regressions (i.e., prioritize routing, caching).
- We have a partial PoC for sampled console traces in staging (Samira ran it). Need eng feedback on sampling heuristics.

Agenda (20–30 min):
- 0–5m: quick contextual sync + wins (what shipped, any urgent incidents)
- 5–12m: deep dive on API latency spike and proposed short-term mitigations (decide A/B/C)
- 12–18m: console tracing retention model and UI surface (decide default retention + premium gating)
- 18–24m: Dedicated burst policy ask — align on guardrails and E2E timeline
- 24–30m: Private onboarding blockers and who owns KMS runbook deliverable
- Wrap: capture decisions, owners, and quick follow-ups

Preparatory material I should bring/ask Diego to review:
- short perf flamegraphs for >4k sequences (link: GitHub PR 987 has artifacts)
- cost model quick calc for console retention (Samira has spreadsheet)
- Dedicated pilot agreement draft (sales) — highlight burst ask and pricing assumptions
- Private onboarding running doc (current state: missing KMS + audit example)

Decision options / my tilt before convo (so I'm not directionless):
- Latency mitigation: slightly lean toward option (B) caching + larger batching with temporary SLO relaxation — less customer-visible than model switch. But be prepared to accept (A) if SLOs still violated.
- Console retention: Default 7d sampling + paid 30d; expose simple per-route override for enterprise seats.
- Dedicated burst: allow burst but require budget cap + billing alert + manual approval threshold at 1.5x baseline.
- Private KMS: ship integration templates + one SDK plugin for AWS KMS in v1, add GCP/Azure HSM examples in v1.1.

Action items to capture during/after 1:1 (I will record in linear/JIRA):
- Diego: quick assessment of feasibility + risk of implementing KV prefetching for long-context requests. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Maya (me): follow up with Sales on Dedicated pilot burst ask, capture pricing expectation and add hard cap language. Due: 2026-03-15.
- Samira: provide retention cost calc and suggested sampling ratio for 7d vs 30d. Due: 2026-03-13 (she already said she would).
- Diego + Platform Eng: draft an ops runbook for burst autoscale (incidents, billing recovery steps). Due: 2026-03-25.
- Maya + Eng: root-cause doc for long seq latency (link back to PR 987 artifacts). Due: 2026-03-20.
- Diego: quick template for KMS integration (AWS example) or recommend vendor SDK to reuse. Due: 2026-03-19.

Follow-up notes (how I'll update):
- After meeting I will: (1) log decisions in the public product roadmap board, (2) create tickets for the agreed action items with owners/due dates, (3) message the relevant Slack channels with short summary + links.

Risk register / escalation triggers to keep in mind:
- If 95th latency stays >1s for >24h for long-context customers, escalate to on-call + product triage and consider temporary rate-limiting.
- If Dedicated burst usage is detected above 1.5x baseline for >48h, auto-throttle and notify sales + customer success.

Loose conversation notes I want to capture live (placeholders):
- Diego reaction to routing vs model swap: __________
- Any SRE red flags re prefetch caching: __________
- Agreement on console UI fields (must-have list): route id, model id, token counts, backend node id, queue wait time, kernel variant

Personal reminders (notes to self):
- Keep meeting under 30 min. Diego likes succinct asks with clear tradeoffs.
- Avoid getting pulled into implementation details; if Diego wants deep dive, schedule follow-up with SRE + runtime owners.
- Bring concrete examples of customer impact (one-liner from acme pilot).

End of prep. Will tidy action items into JIRA after the meeting and update this doc with outcomes.

Quick revision history (for transparency):
- 2026-02-09: initial draft
- 2026-03-05: updated numbers and added Dedicated pilot details
- 2026-03-11: final pre-meeting touch (added due dates and linked artifacts)
